#[repr(C)] — Rust does not guarantee field order otherwise
The struct has to be declared pub for the C side
writing.exampleCaption: A declaration, a layout guarantee, and one unsafe call.
writing.explanation: extern "C" selects the C calling convention and #[repr(C)] fixes field order so a struct matches its C counterpart. Every call is unsafe because the compiler cannot see the other side, and ownership must be agreed explicitly — who allocates, who frees, and how long a borrowed pointer stays valid.
writing.feedback: Without repr(C) the layout is unspecified and the C side may read the wrong bytes.
